events.objective: Establish the symptom timeline for notification-service: exact times of each OOMKilled restart this week and memory usage trend (working set / heap) leading into each. Determine whether the third OOM is a deviation in trend or a repeat of an existing pattern. Report onset time of the first anomaly, whether consumer lag spikes precede or follow OOM restarts, and confirm which services actually show anomalies in the same window (error signatures, OOMs, latency, lag).

Find what changed across ALL services in the days before and around the incident: list recent deployments, config changes (especially notification-service consumer/Kafka settings, JVM/heap, resource limits), and the Kafka maintenance details. Map notification-service's service dependencies and shared components (Kafka brokers, other consumers on the same topic, shared DB/cache), and search historical incidents for prior OOMKilled or Kafka-replay patterns affecting notification-service or its topic peers.

Correlate the changes and dependency findings from task b against the onset/restart times found in task a: identify which specific change (if any) aligns with the first OOM and each subsequent restart this week, and whether the Kafka maintenance timing explains the latest event better than the pre-existing pattern. Assess whether a shared dependency change affects other services too.

events.statement: Only one notification-service deployment in the 7 days before the incident: dep-5402 v3.8.0 at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z adding an in-memory template cache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment on the email render path); status live, rolled_back_t null. It landed ~2.5 days before the report.

The only other deployment across all services in the window is unrelated auth-service v7.1.4 (patch, jackson bump) at 2026-03-22T13:00:00Z; the deployment query returned count=2 for scope 'all services' and was not partial.

Exactly one config change in the window and it is the Kafka maintenance: kafka log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000 (7d -> 3d) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z by platform-team, i.e. ~2h20m before the 20:20Z incident report. No notification-service consumer/JVM/heap/resource-limit config change appears in the results.

notification-service's direct dependencies are kafka (queue-consume) and email-provider (external, no telemetry); notification-service itself is not shared. Kafka is the SHARED component (shared: true, owner platform) whose peers are order-service and payment-service (queue-produce) and settlement-service (queue-consume), plus api-gateway -> order/payment over HTTP — so settlement-service is the other consumer on the shared topic.

A depth-2 upstream query on notification-service returned no incoming edges (empty edges array) — no service calls notification-service; its load arrives only by consuming from the shared kafka topic.

Prior incident HIST-104 (2025-11-05) matches the same symptom pair — consumer lag spike + delayed emails on notification-service/kafka — with root cause 'Partition reassignment caused consumer group rebalancing storm' (category infrastructure_failure, throttled reassignment). HIST-107 (redis cold-cache storm) matched only weakly (score 1). These are leads about similar symptoms, not evidence about this incident's cause.

events.description: No notification-service consumer/Kafka-consumer-group, JVM/heap (Xmx) or container resource-limit config change appeared in get_config_changes for 2026-03-16..23; only 1 change returned (count=1, not partial), so either none exist or such settings are not tracked there. Cannot confirm whether heap/limit tuning accompanied dep-5402.
email-provider has has_telemetry=false, and no metrics were queried for notification-service/kafka (no time-series pull was done with the remaining budget).
Historical search returned only 2 incidents (HIST-104, HIST-107); no prior HIST entry with literal 'OOMKilled' for notification-service was retrievable.

events.answer: In the window 2026-03-16..23 the only service deployments were notification-service v3.8.0 ("Add in-memory template cache for email rendering", 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, live, not rolled back) and an unrelated auth-service jackson bump. The single config change was the Kafka maintenance: kafka log.retention.ms reduced 604800000 -> 259200000 (7d -> 3d) at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z, ~2h20m before the 20:20Z report. notification-service consumes from the SHARED kafka broker, whose other peers are order-service and payment-service (producers) and settlement-service (consumer), plus api-gateway->order/payment HTTP. Precedent HIST-104 (2025-11-05) shows the same symptom pair (consumer lag spike, delayed emails) caused by Kafka broker rebalance/partition reassignment.

events.statement: Exactly three OOMKilled restarts (exit code 137) of notification-service-7d9f occurred in this week's window, at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z — closely spaced near 22:00/20:00 daily, roughly 24h apart.
The restarts metric (cumulative) confirms three restarts: it steps from 0 to 1 in the 2026-03-21T22:00 bucket, to 2 in the 2026-03-22T22:00 bucket, and to 3 in the 2026-03-23T20:00 bucket.

memory_pct shows a sawtooth ramp-then-crash pattern preceding every OOM: it climbs steadily (~48% -> 95%+) and resets to ~48% at each restart. First OOM (03-21T22:59) was preceded by a ramp from 48.23% at 03-21T00:00 to avg 92.91/max 95.09 at 03-21T20:00 and max 97.37 at 03-21T22:00. Second (03-22T21:59) ramped 50.33 -> avg 94.91/max 97.98 at 03-22T20:00. Third (03-23T19:59) ramped 52.99 -> avg 95.05/max 98.44 at 03-23T18:00 with 20-min buckets reaching avg 96.73/max 98.44 at 19:40, then resetting to 46.72 at 20:00.

The first anomaly in the week is NOT the OOM: log warnings begin 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z with 'GC pause 253ms exceeded 200ms target', and the memory_pct ramp clearly begins in the 2026-03-21T02:00 bucket (avg 52.71) after a flat ~48% baseline on 03-20; heap-over-90% 'full GC took' warnings start at 2026-03-21T21:37:01Z, just before the first OOM.

consumer_lag spikes immediately AFTER each memory crash/OOM, not before: during the ramps lag stays in its normal ~50-100 band, then jumps within the same/next bucket — 03-21T22:00 avg 2273.11/max 17161.92; 03-22T20:00 avg 790.21/max 17611.66 and 22:00 avg 1589.77/max 14375.74; 03-23 the 19:40 bucket avg 4578.25/max 18137.93 while memory is already at 96.73%.

The third OOM is a repeat of the same pattern, not a deviation: memory ramps to the same ~95-98% ceiling and collapses, identical sawtooth shape as the 03-21 and 03-22 events, and the first heap-over-90% warning in each ramp comes just minutes before the OOM (e.g. 03-23 ramp warnings from 18:34:46Z, OOM at 19:59:21Z). The reported causal link to 'today's Kafka maintenance' is not supported by the data: the lag spike follows the crash, and the ramp began the prior day.

No heap/working-set absolute bytes metric was available; only memory_pct. available_metrics for notification-service lists memory_pct, cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, request_rate, consumer_lag, restarts.

events.answer: notification-service had three OOMKilled restarts (exit 137) this week: 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z, 2026-03-22T21:59:47Z, and 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, each preceded by the same ~24h memory sawtooth ramp from ~48% to ~95-98% (a repeating pattern, not a new deviation). The first anomaly of the week is the memory ramp itself, starting in the 2026-03-21T02:00 bucket (with a GC-pause warning at 03:00:44Z), i.e. ~21h before the first OOM — not the Kafka maintenance. Consumer lag spikes immediately AFTER each crash/restart, not before (e.g. lag 2273 avg at 03-21T22:00 right at the OOM, and 4578 avg at 03-23T19:40 while memory was already at 96.7%).

events.statement: Across 2026-03-16..24 the ONLY notification-service deployment is dep-5402 v3.8.0 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z (status live, rolled_back_at null) — it is the only notification-service change preceding the first OOM at 2026-03-21T22:59:50Z (~23h earlier).

There is NOT a single configuration/flag change on notification-service in the window (scope=notification-service returns count=0, not partial); the sole config change anywhere is the Kafka maintenance.

The Kafka maintenance cfg-2410 (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000, i.e. 7d -> 3d, platform-team) is timestamped 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z — ~2h before the third OOM (19:59:21Z) and ~19h after the memory ramp for that cycle already began (~03-22T21:00). Retention is a stored-data window change, not a consumer/broker-capacity change.

No code deployment at all occurred on 2026-03-23 (12:00-24:00 window, all services: count=0, not partial), so nothing was shipped in the ~12h before the third OOM; the last deployment of any kind was the unrelated auth-service jackson bump on 03-22T13:00Z.

Kafka is a SHARED component (shared: true, owner platform) and settlement-service is a peer consumer on it (settlement-service -> kafka queue-consume, plus settlement-service -> ledger-db); notification-service's other direct dependency is email-provider (external, no telemetry). A shared-Kafka change therefore COULD reach settlement-service, but the retention reduction is the only Kafka change and neither settlement-service nor the other peers (order-service, payment-service) is reported with OOM symptoms.

The only historical precedent matching the symptom pair (lag spike + delayed emails) is HIST-104 (2025-11-05), attributed to a Kafka broker rebalance/partition-reassignment storm — a lead, and notably a broker-side event with NO deployment/config change, i.e. a different class of cause than a code change. No prior OOMKilled/memory-ramp incident for notification-service was found.

events.description: No metric telemetry confirms whether dep-5402's TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) is the source of the unbounded memory growth; correlation is by timing/elimination only, not by attribution to the cache at runtime.

Kafka broker-side events (partition reassignment/rebalance, as in HIST-104) are not queryable via the config/deployment tools; absence of a config record does not exclude a broker-side rebalance around 03-21..03-23.

No deployment/config change is recorded between 2026-03-21T00:00Z and 03-23T12:00Z besides the Kafka retention change, so no change explains the difference between the 03-21, 03-22 and 03-23 restart times; they appear to be the same repeating cycle.

events.answer: The only change that precedes all three restarts is notification-service deployment dep-5402 v3.8.0 (in-memory template cache) at 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z, ~23h before the FIRST OOM (03-21T22:59:50Z) and before the first memory ramp bucket (03-21T02:00). It aligns with the first OOM and, since it is the sole notification-service change all week, remains the best-fitting origin for the repeating pattern that produced all three restarts. The Kafka maintenance (kafka log.retention.ms 7d->3d at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z) starts only ~2h before the third OOM and ~19h into an already-ramping sawtooth, so it does NOT explain the latest event better than the pre-existing pattern — lag spikes follow the crashes, not precede them. Kafka is a shared component (also consumed by settlement-service, produced by order-service/payment-service), but the change was a retention reduction affecting stored data, and no other service shows the notification-service OOM signature.
